chapter: Day two: mother, reading, LSU writing
title: Collingwood again: seeing Black culture as art
summary: Allison says Collingwood helped him see that what he had grown up with was art.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: I watched a couple of the movies that have been made about you... I’d like also to discuss a bit more about when you got to LSU and were introduced to R.A. Collingwood’s book on aesthetics and art. Now, in a film I was looking at this morning, you said, “It made me aware that a lot of the things that I had been doing were artistic, or at least headed in that direction,” and that reading that book and thinking about what Collingwood was writing helped you understand that black culture was art.
Whereas before it had just been what was around you.
Yes, pretty much. I remember Collingwood stimulated me to a lot of thoughts about art. I remember he had a theory of art, he had a saying about art, and... What’s that...I don’t know...
There’s a book in there with all your underlinings in it.
Shall I run and get the book?
That would be great. Let’s see some of the things your dad underlined. But I know
one thing that you paid attention to was Walter Pater’s remark that “art is the removal of surpluses.” That struck you.
Yeah. Well, that’s one of the things that struck me.
I remember you said to me at one time that it was the honest expression of an honest emotion, that it was really about no false...
